name: voxbind
description: Turn one person's WhatsApp voice notes into a memoir: Voxbind keeps only the chosen person's notes from a chat export, transcribes and dates them, groups them into chapters with ChatGPT, and makes listening pages that play their original voice. In the United States and Canada it also prints a 6 x 9 inch hardcover whose QR codes play that voice.

interface.shortDescription: Their voice notes, as a memoir
interface.longDescription:
Voxbind is a memory book of one person's voice messages: it turns their WhatsApp voice notes into a memoir, every note transcribed and dated, grouped into chapters, with listening pages that play their own voice.

How it works:
1. In WhatsApp, open the chat and choose Export chat with media (Attach Media on iPhone, Include media on Android).
2. Attach the ZIP in ChatGPT and ask for a memoir. Voxbind lists who sent voice notes and how many; you choose one person and confirm you may use their recordings.
3. Voxbind keeps only that person's voice notes and deletes everything else in the export straight away. It transcribes each note in the language it was spoken.
4. ChatGPT reads the transcripts and suggests chapter titles in the person's own words. Fix a misheard word or leave a note out in the card.

The printed book (United States and Canada only): a 6 x 9 inch hardcover with a contents page, dated chapters, the transcript of every note under its date, and a QR code at the start of each chapter. Any phone camera opens a private page that plays the original recordings, with no app or account. The back cover holds a code for the whole archive. Preview every page in the chat, then order it; the address and payment are entered on voxbind.ambientapp.ai. Printed and shipped to the United States and Canada only. Everywhere else, the memoir, transcripts, listening pages and recordings download work the same, without the printed book.

Also works with recordings from a phone's voice recorder (m4a, mp3, wav, ogg, opus). Exports too large to attach, or attachments that don't come through, go in on a private upload page.

Privacy:
- Only the person you choose is kept. The chat text, photos and videos in the export are deleted as soon as it is read, and other people's voice notes when you choose, or after two hours if you don't.
- No voiceprints: Voxbind knows who sent each note from the names in the export, never by analysing anyone's voice. It never imitates or clones a voice.
- Audio stays on Voxbind's server; ChatGPT receives only the names in the export and, after you choose, the transcripts.
- Delete a memoir at any time: say "Delete my Voxbind memoir".

Limits:
- Up to 600 voice notes per memoir.
- Printed books (United States and Canada) have 24 to 320 pages; notes in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew or other scripts the book can't print yet stay in the memoir and play on their listening pages.
- Not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta.
capabilities: Turn one person's voice notes into a memoir
Transcribe and date every note into chapters
Listening pages that play their original voice
Printed hardcover with QR codes in the US and Canada
defaultPrompt: Turn Grandma's WhatsApp voice notes into a memoir
Keep my late grandmother's voice messages in a memoir the family can hear
Show me a sample Voxbind memoir

positive.description: See what Voxbind makes, with nothing to attach. No sign-in is needed: Voxbind has no accounts, and each ChatGPT user has their own memoirs, so you start with none. Run first, in a new chat. The sample is a made-up grandmother, Nana Mae, whose voice notes were made with a synthetic voice; the card and the listening page say so.
positive.prompt: Show me a sample Voxbind memoir
positive.expected_behavior: A card shows Nana Mae, In Her Own Words: 6 chapters with their dates (tap one to see each note with a player and its transcript) and the book's 24 pages (the pages show for users in the United States and Canada; elsewhere the card shows the chapters and the listening page only). The reply says the person is made up and the voice is synthetic. Tapping Listening page opens voxbind.ambientapp.ai/v/... with her chapters; each chapter there plays her voice.

positive.description: Import a WhatsApp export. Download the test export from the attachment link (a 260 KB ZIP exported from a made-up chat between Nana Mae and her granddaughter Ella, with synthetic voices) and attach it with this prompt. ChatGPT may show 'Allow ChatGPT to use Memory Book of Voice Messages?' first, because the export's chat text, photos and videos are deleted once it has been read; choose Allow once. ChatGPT sees the names of the people in the export, never the recordings or the chat text. If the ZIP doesn't reach Voxbind from the chat, the reply and the card give a private upload page on voxbind.ambientapp.ai instead: open it, add the same ZIP there, then come back to this chat for case 3.
positive.prompt: Turn my grandmother Nana Mae's WhatsApp voice notes into a book. The export is attached.
positive.expected_behavior: Either way, nothing is kept or transcribed yet, and the export's people are listed: voice notes from 2 people, Nana Mae (8 voice notes, Mar 2021 to Jan 2024) and Ella (2), with the consent statement word for word. When the ZIP comes through, ChatGPT lists them, asks whose voice the book should keep, and the card offers the two people and a consent box. When it doesn't, ChatGPT says the export didn't come through and gives the upload page (the card shows an Open the upload page button); once the ZIP is added there, the page and the card list the same two people with the consent box.

positive.description: Choose the person and confirm consent. Run after case 2, in the same chat; it works the same after the upload page (choose_speaker takes the export waiting for a choice). ChatGPT may show 'Allow ChatGPT to use Memory Book of Voice Messages?' first, because this deletes the rest of the export and makes unlisted listening pages; choose Allow once. Transcription takes about a minute for the 8 notes; ask 'Is it done?' if the card still shows progress.
positive.prompt: Keep Nana Mae's voice notes. I confirm the statement: they are my grandmother's and she agreed.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT says it kept 8 voice notes from Nana Mae and deleted everything else in the export (if Nana Mae was already chosen on the upload page, it says her voice notes are already in the memoir). The card shows transcription progress, then dated chapters; opening one shows each note with a player and its transcript. Ella's notes are not in the memoir.

positive.description: Shape the chapters from the transcripts. Run after case 3, once the memoir is ready.
positive.prompt: Read her transcripts and give the chapters good titles from what she talks about.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads the transcripts (the farm and the rooster, meeting her husband, the peach cobbler, Christmas, the telephone exchange, advice, a new year) and sets titled chapters that start at note 1 and follow the dates. Titles use her own subjects and add no facts. The card shows the new titles.

positive.description: Preview and order the book. Run after case 4, from the United States or Canada: printing is offered only there, by ChatGPT's user location. From another country preview_book and order_book reply that printed books aren't available in the user's country, and the card shows the memoir with no book or order step. ChatGPT may ask before ordering. The checkout page is on voxbind.ambientapp.ai: enter the promotion code VOXBIND-DE2D03A7 there, with any US address, to pay $0. A $0 order goes to the printer's test system, so nothing is printed or charged. To finish, say "Delete my Voxbind memoir".
positive.prompt: Preview the book, then order one printed copy.
positive.expected_behavior: The card shows the book's pages (title, how to listen, contents, chapters with QR codes and transcripts). The reply gives the page count and a secure checkout link on voxbind.ambientapp.ai where the address, copies and payment are entered; nothing is charged in ChatGPT. Ordering again for the same copies returns the same order.

negative.description: General advice about backing up chats. ChatGPT answers itself.
negative.prompt: How do I back up my WhatsApp chats to Google Drive?
negative.expected_behavior: No Voxbind tool is called. ChatGPT explains WhatsApp's own backup.

negative.description: Imitating a voice. Voxbind only keeps and plays original recordings; it never clones or imitates a voice.
negative.prompt: Make an audio message that sounds like my grandmother's voice saying happy birthday.

negative.description: Summarising a chat. Voxbind makes books of voice notes, not chat summaries.
negative.prompt: Summarize what my family group chat talked about this week.
negative.expected_behavior: No Voxbind tool is called. ChatGPT answers itself or asks for the chat text.

review.commerce_description: Voxbind sells one physical product: a printed 6 x 9 inch hardcover of the user's memoir, printed and shipped by Lulu to the United States and Canada. The printed book is offered only to users in the United States and Canada (by ChatGPT's user location): elsewhere Voxbind shows no price, book preview, checkout or order step, and the memoir, transcripts and listening pages work without it. order_book returns a link to an external checkout on voxbind.ambientapp.ai (Stripe), where the address, number of copies and payment are entered; nothing is charged in ChatGPT and no card data passes through the plugin. There are no subscriptions, credits or digital goods for sale, and the price is the same in ChatGPT and on the website.

publication.release_notes: Now listed in every country: the memoir, transcripts, chapters and listening pages work everywhere, and the printed book is offered only in the United States and Canada, where it ships (elsewhere the card and replies leave the book, its cost and the order step out; print tools gain a print_available field). Listing: renamed Memory Book of Voice Messages, with the subtitle "Their voice notes, as a memoir"; search words for memory books, voice messages, life story books, voice memos and voicemails; capabilities say what the memoir and the book do; a new icon with a dark-mode version; the starter prompts name the memoir, which works in every country. Adds three skills: voice memoir, voice notes into chapters and the hardcover. Tool descriptions now name keeping a loved one's voice messages and recordings from a phone's voice recorder (m4a). Server instructions and tool descriptions describe the memoir first, with the printed book as the United States and Canada option, and only the hardcover skill names the printed book. No change to tool names.
